items.stem:
This question is about transport in plants: xylem and phloem.

(a) Explain the mechanism of translocation in phloem. [3]

(b) Briefly describe ringing experiments on woody stems and explain what it reveals about the role of phloem in translocation. [3]
items.answer: (a) At the source, sucrose is actively loaded into companion cells/sieve tubes; water potential falls; water enters from xylem by osmosis; hydrostatic pressure rises; sap flows towards sinks where sucrose is unloaded and used/stored; water leaves, lowering pressure (pressure-flow). (b) Removing a ring of bark causes swelling above the ring as sugars accumulate. Phloem lies in the bark; cutting it stops downward transport of sugar while xylem transport continues.
items.markingKey: (a) [3] Award marks for: At the source, sucrose is actively loaded into companion cells/sieve tubes; water potential falls; water enters from xylem by osmosis; hydrostatic pressure rises; sap flows towards sinks where sucrose is unloaded and used/stored; water leaves, lowering pressure (pressure-flow). Award up to 3 marks for valid, linked points. (b) [3] Context (Removing a ring of bark causes swelling above the ring as sugars accumulate.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Phloem lies in the bark; cutting it stops downward transport of sugar while xylem transport continues. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to the role of phloem in translocation. Award up to 3 marks for valid, linked points.

items.stem:
This question is about gas exchange surfaces: lungs, ventilation and alveoli.

(a) Explain how the structure of alveoli is adapted for gas exchange. [2]

(b) Outline one way in which emphysema in long-term smokers shows the importance of alveolar structure for gas exchange. [4]
items.answer: (a) Very large total surface area; walls of thin type I pneumocytes and capillary endothelium give short diffusion distance (about 0.5 µm); moist lining dissolves gases; dense capillary network with continuous blood flow maintains gradients; surfactant prevents collapse. (b) Elastase from inflammatory cells breaks down elastin in alveolar walls, which merge into large air spaces. Reduced surface area and loss of elastic recoil lower the efficiency of gas exchange and ventilation.
items.markingKey: (a) [2] Award marks for: Very large total surface area; walls of thin type I pneumocytes and capillary endothelium give short diffusion distance (about 0.5 µm); moist lining dissolves gases; dense capillary network with continuous blood flow maintains gradients; surfactant prevents collapse. Award up to 2 marks for valid, linked points. (b) [4] Context (Elastase from inflammatory cells breaks down elastin in alveolar walls, which merge into large air spaces.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Reduced surface area and loss of elastic recoil lower the efficiency of gas exchange and ventilation. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to the importance of alveolar structure for gas exchange. Award up to 4 marks for valid, linked points.

items.stem:
This question is about blood vessels, capillaries and tissue fluid; the heart and cardiac cycle.

(a) Which vessels have valves to prevent backflow? [1]

(b) Explain how the heartbeat is initiated and coordinated. [2]

(c) An ECG of Lars shows that the time between successive R waves is 0.68 s. Calculate the heart rate in beats per minute. The stroke volume is 73 cm³. Calculate the cardiac output in dm³ min⁻¹. [3]
items.answer: (a) veins (b) The SA node (pacemaker) depolarises spontaneously, sending impulses across both atria, which contract; the AV node delays the impulse; it passes down the bundle of His and Purkinje fibres to the ventricle apex, so ventricles contract from the bottom up, after atria have emptied. (c) 88 beats min⁻¹; 6.44 dm³ min⁻¹
items.markingKey: (a) [1] veins. Low pressure in veins. Award up to 1 mark for valid, linked points. (b) [2] Award marks for: The SA node (pacemaker) depolarises spontaneously, sending impulses across both atria, which contract; the AV node delays the impulse; it passes down the bundle of His and Purkinje fibres to the ventricle apex, so ventricles contract from the bottom up, after atria have emptied. Award up to 2 marks for valid, linked points. (c) [3] 60/0.68 = 88 (A1); 73 × 88.2 = 6441 cm³ (M1) = 6.44 dm³ min⁻¹ (A1). Award up to 3 marks for valid, linked points.

items.stem:
This question is about karyotypes, genome size and whole-genome sequencing.

(a) Which plant has one of the largest known genomes (about 149 billion base pairs)? [1]

(b) Explain the uses of whole-genome sequencing. [2]

(c) Hybrids can be produced between two closely related species of goat with diploid numbers 34 and 30. State the chromosome number of the hybrid and explain why it is likely to be infertile. [3]
items.answer: (a) Paris japonica (b) Comparing genomes reveals evolutionary relationships and common ancestry; identifies genes and mutations linked to disease; allows personalised medicine; helps classification and conservation genetics; has become faster and cheaper since the Human Genome Project. (c) 32; chromosomes cannot all pair as homologues in meiosis, so gametes are unbalanced
items.markingKey: (a) [1] Paris japonica. Genome size does not correlate with complexity. Award up to 1 mark for valid, linked points. (b) [2] Award marks for: Comparing genomes reveals evolutionary relationships and common ancestry; identifies genes and mutations linked to disease; allows personalised medicine; helps classification and conservation genetics; has become faster and cheaper since the Human Genome Project. Award up to 2 marks for valid, linked points. (c) [3] 17 + 15 = 32 (A1); chromosomes from different species are not homologous / odd or unmatched set cannot pair in meiosis I (R1); gametes have incomplete sets (R1). Award up to 3 marks for valid, linked points.

items.stem:
This question is about viruses: structure, lytic and lysogenic cycles.

(a) Distinguish between enveloped viruses and non-enveloped viruses. [2]

(b) A suspension of a phage used in phage therapy trials was diluted by a factor of 10⁶. 0.2 cm³ of the diluted suspension was spread with E. coli on an agar plate and 155 plaques formed. Calculate the concentration of infective phage particles in the original suspension, in plaque-forming units (pfu) per cm³. [4]
items.answer: (a) Enveloped viruses (e.g. HIV, influenza) have an outer membrane derived from the host plasma membrane with viral glycoproteins; non-enveloped viruses (e.g. T4) have only a protein capsid. (b) 7.75 × 10⁸ pfu cm⁻³
items.markingKey: (a) [2] Enveloped viruses (e.g. HIV, influenza) have an outer membrane derived from the host plasma membrane with viral glycoproteins; non-enveloped viruses (e.g. T4) have only a protein capsid. Award up to 2 marks for valid, linked points. (b) [4] pfu cm⁻³ = plaques ÷ (volume × dilution) = 155 ÷ (0.2 × 10⁻6) (M1) = 7.75 × 10⁸ (A1). Award up to 4 marks for valid, linked points.

items.stem:
This question is about organelles and compartmentalization; separation of nucleus and cytoplasm.

(a) Explain the difference between ribosomes bound to rough ER and free ribosomes. [3]

(b) Briefly describe pancreatic acinar cells secreting digestive enzymes and explain what it reveals about the secretory pathway and compartmentalisation. [3]
items.answer: (a) Free ribosomes make proteins used within the cytoplasm; ribosomes on rough ER make proteins that enter the ER for secretion, insertion in membranes or delivery to lysosomes. (b) Radioactive amino acids traced by Palade appeared first in rough ER, then the Golgi, then secretory vesicles. The sequence of organelles shows how proteins are made, processed and packaged in separate compartments.

(b) Using the Amazon rainforest as an example, explain biodiversity at ecosystem, species and genetic levels. [5]

items.stem:
This question is about structure-function of mitochondria and chloroplasts.

(a) With the help of a specific example, explain how the structure of the chloroplast is adapted to photosynthesis. [4]

(b) Noah writes: "Chloroplasts are found in all plant cells and produce all their ATP." Explain why this is inaccurate. [5]

(c) Compare the structure of mitochondria and chloroplasts and explain how each is adapted to its function. [7]
items.answer: (a) Thylakoid membranes stacked in grana give large area for photosystems and pigments; small thylakoid lumen accumulates protons for chemiosmosis; stroma contains Calvin cycle enzymes (rubisco) close to the products of light reactions; starch grains store products; own DNA and ribosomes. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (b) Many plant cells (e.g. roots) lack chloroplasts; plant cells use mitochondria for respiratory ATP; chloroplast ATP is mainly used in the Calvin cycle. (c) Both: double membrane, own DNA, 70S ribosomes, internal membranes with ATP synthase, proton gradients. Mitochondria: cristae, matrix (Krebs), small intermembrane space. Chloroplasts: thylakoids/grana with pigments, lumen, stroma (Calvin), starch grains. Adaptations explained.

items.stem: How many strands does a typical mRNA molecule have?
options: one
three
four
two
items.answer: one
items.markingKey: A. mRNA is single-stranded; DNA is usually double-stranded.

items.stem: Which statement about habitats, adaptations and abiotic variables is not correct?
options: Animals develop adaptations during their lifetime because they need them.
Adaptation is a heritable characteristic that increases an organism’s chance of survival and reproduction in its environment.
A habitat is the place where an organism lives.
Xerophytes are adapted to dry conditions (conserving water).
items.answer: Animals develop adaptations during their lifetime because they need them.
items.markingKey: A. The incorrect statement is “Animals develop adaptations during their lifetime because they need them.” – Adaptations arise by natural selection on heritable variation over generations; individuals do not develop them in response to need.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "thermophile"?
options: The association of two or more polypeptide subunits (and sometimes prosthetic groups) into a functional protein
The pH at which a protein (such as an enzyme) is most stable and active
The sequence of amino acids in a polypeptide, determined by the base sequence of a gene
An organism adapted to live at high temperatures, with proteins that remain stable when hot
items.answer: An organism adapted to live at high temperatures, with proteins that remain stable when hot
items.markingKey: D. "thermophile" is an organism adapted to live at high temperatures, with proteins that remain stable when hot.

items.stem: Runners can lose over 1 litre of sweat per hour, which evaporates from the skin. Which concept is best illustrated by this example (sweating in marathon runners in hot climates)?
options: Cohesion and adhesion in water transport
The testing of hypotheses about the origin of Earth’s water
The high latent heat of vaporisation of water
Surface tension
items.answer: The high latent heat of vaporisation of water
items.markingKey: C. Each gram evaporated absorbs about 2.4 kJ, so evaporative cooling removes a large amount of metabolic heat.

items.stem: Which statement about structure-function of mitochondria and chloroplasts is not correct?
options: Chloroplasts are found in all plant cells and produce all their ATP.
Cristae is the folds of the inner mitochondrial membrane, which increase the surface area for electron transport and ATP synthase.
Intermembrane space is the narrow space between the inner and outer mitochondrial membranes where protons accumulate.
Stroma is the fluid surrounding the thylakoids in a chloroplast, containing enzymes of the Calvin cycle.
items.answer: Chloroplasts are found in all plant cells and produce all their ATP.
items.markingKey: A. The incorrect statement is “Chloroplasts are found in all plant cells and produce all their ATP.” – Many plant cells (e.g. roots) lack chloroplasts; plant cells use mitochondria for respiratory ATP; chloroplast ATP is mainly used in the Calvin cycle.

items.stem: Which antigens are present on the red blood cells of a person with blood group AB?
options: both A and B antigens
B antigen only
neither A nor B antigen
A antigen only
items.answer: both A and B antigens
items.markingKey: A. AB has both glycoprotein modifications.

items.stem: Why is the bilayer a barrier to ions and polar molecules?
options: It is made of protein.
Its heads are hydrophobic.
It is completely impermeable to everything.
Its hydrophobic core does not allow charged or polar particles to pass easily.
items.answer: Its hydrophobic core does not allow charged or polar particles to pass easily.
items.markingKey: D. Small non-polar molecules pass easily; ions need proteins.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The tendency of the surface of a liquid to resist an external force, caused by cohesion between surface molecules"?
options: surface tension
thermal conductivity
capillary action
Goldilocks zone
items.answer: surface tension
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of surface tension.

items.stem: Neighbouring populations interbreed, but the two end populations in the south coexist without interbreeding. Which concept is best illustrated by this example (the ring of Ensatina salamanders around the Central Valley of California)?
options: How cladistics leads to reclassification
Cladistics using molecular and morphological evidence
The three-domain system of classification
The limitations of the biological species concept
items.answer: The limitations of the biological species concept
items.markingKey: D. Speciation is gradual, so there may be no clear point at which populations become separate species.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about range of tolerance, transects and biomes is false?
options: The optimum is usually in the middle of the range.
Range of tolerance is the range of values of an abiotic factor within which a species can survive, with an optimum range in which it thrives.
A correlation between light intensity and fern abundance proves that light causes the distribution.
A line transect records organisms touching a line at intervals.
items.answer: A correlation between light intensity and fern abundance proves that light causes the distribution.
items.markingKey: C. The incorrect statement is “A correlation between light intensity and fern abundance proves that light causes the distribution.” – Correlation does not prove causation; other factors (e.g. soil moisture) may vary with light; experiments are needed to test causation.

items.stem: What is the advantage of separating transcription in the nucleus from translation in the cytoplasm?
options: ribosomes can enter the nucleus
translation is faster in the nucleus
mRNA can be modified (e.g. intron removal) before translation
DNA can be translated directly
items.answer: mRNA can be modified (e.g. intron removal) before translation
items.markingKey: C. Prokaryotes translate mRNA while it is still being transcribed.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about simple diffusion, facilitated diffusion and osmosis is false?
options: Facilitated diffusion uses ATP because proteins are involved.
Simple diffusion is the net passive movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration, directly through the phospholipid bilayer.
Water moves from a region of lower solute concentration (higher water potential) to higher solute concentration (lower water potential).
Isotonic is describes a solution with the same solute concentration (osmolarity) as the cell, so there is no net movement of water.
items.answer: Facilitated diffusion uses ATP because proteins are involved.
items.markingKey: A. The incorrect statement is “Facilitated diffusion uses ATP because proteins are involved.” – Facilitated diffusion is passive and uses no ATP; it is active transport that uses ATP.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "endocytosis"?
options: An ion channel that opens or closes in response to changes in membrane potential, e.g. sodium and potassium channels in axons
A steroid found between phospholipids in animal membranes that regulates fluidity and reduces permeability to small polar molecules
The uptake of material into a cell by the plasma membrane folding inwards to form a vesicle
An ion channel that opens when a specific chemical (ligand) binds, e.g. the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor
items.answer: The uptake of material into a cell by the plasma membrane folding inwards to form a vesicle
items.markingKey: C. "endocytosis" is the uptake of material into a cell by the plasma membrane folding inwards to form a vesicle.

items.stem: Athletes “carbo-load” to raise muscle glycogen; during races glycogen is rapidly hydrolysed for respiration. Which concept is best illustrated by this example (muscle glycogen stores in endurance athletes)?
options: Glycogen as an energy store
The roles of triglycerides
Hydrolysis reactions
Lipids as energy stores
items.answer: Glycogen as an energy store
items.markingKey: A. Highly branched glycogen provides many ends for rapid release of glucose when demand is high.

items.stem: Which statement about blood vessels, capillaries and tissue fluid; the heart and cardiac cycle is not correct?
options: Sinoatrial node is the pacemaker of the heart: a group of specialised cardiac muscle cells in the right atrium that initiates each heartbeat.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart at high pressure, with thick muscular elastic walls and narrow lumens.
Cardiac cycle is the sequence of events in one heartbeat, including atrial and ventricular systole and diastole.
Veins always carry deoxygenated blood.
items.answer: Veins always carry deoxygenated blood.
items.markingKey: D. The incorrect statement is “Veins always carry deoxygenated blood.” – Veins carry blood towards the heart; the pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs.

items.stem: Which species has a diploid chromosome number of 48?
options: chimpanzee
human
fruit fly
domestic dog
items.answer: chimpanzee
items.markingKey: A. Human chromosome 2 formed from the fusion of two ancestral chromosomes.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about classification hierarchy and the three domains is false?
options: Domain is the highest taxonomic rank; all life is classified into three domains: Archaea, Bacteria and Eukarya.
Taxon is a group of organisms at any level of the classification hierarchy, such as a genus or family.
Taxonomy is the science of naming, describing and classifying organisms.
Organisms in the same order are more closely related than those in the same genus.
items.answer: Organisms in the same order are more closely related than those in the same genus.
items.markingKey: D. The incorrect statement is “Organisms in the same order are more closely related than those in the same genus.” – The genus is a lower, more specific taxon; members of a genus are more closely related than members of an order.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "stem cell"?
options: The separation of organelles by homogenising cells and centrifuging at increasing speeds (differential centrifugation)
The process by which unspecialised cells become specialised for a particular function by expressing particular genes
An unspecialised cell that can divide repeatedly and differentiate into specialised cell types
A stack of thylakoids in a chloroplast
items.answer: An unspecialised cell that can divide repeatedly and differentiate into specialised cell types
items.markingKey: C. "stem cell" is an unspecialised cell that can divide repeatedly and differentiate into specialised cell types.

items.stem: Within weeks, cryo-EM revealed the spike protein’s shape at near-atomic resolution. Which concept is best illustrated by this example (the use of cryogenic electron microscopy to determine the structure of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in 2020)?
options: The RNA world hypothesis
How conditions on early Earth may have produced organic molecules
The lytic cycle
How developments in microscopy improve biological understanding
items.answer: How developments in microscopy improve biological understanding
items.markingKey: D. Rapid freezing preserves the native structure and the short electron wavelength gives very high resolution, supporting vaccine design.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about adaptive radiation and polyploidy is false?
options: Autopolyploidy is polyploidy in which the extra chromosome sets come from the same species, e.g. by failure of chromosomes to separate in meiosis.
Autopolyploidy involves extra sets of chromosomes from the same species (e.g. through non-disjunction).
Hybrid sterility is the inability of a hybrid between two species to produce viable gametes, usually because its chromosomes cannot pair in meiosis.
Adaptive radiation is the same as convergent evolution.
items.answer: Adaptive radiation is the same as convergent evolution.
items.markingKey: D. The incorrect statement is “Adaptive radiation is the same as convergent evolution.” – Adaptive radiation is divergence from one ancestor into many forms; convergent evolution is unrelated lineages becoming similar.

items.stem: Which bacteriophage is the classic example of the lysogenic cycle?
options: influenza virus
lambda (λ) phage
T4 phage
HIV
items.answer: lambda (λ) phage
items.markingKey: B. λ integrates into the E. coli chromosome.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about ecological niches: obligate and facultative modes of nutrition is false?
options: Mixotroph is an organism that can use both autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition, such as Euglena.
Ecological niche is the role of a species in an ecosystem, including its habitat, its use of resources and all its interactions with other species and abiotic factors.
The niche of a species is the same as its habitat.
Obligate anaerobe is an organism that can only survive in the absence of oxygen, for which oxygen is toxic.
items.answer: The niche of a species is the same as its habitat.
items.markingKey: C. The incorrect statement is “The niche of a species is the same as its habitat.” – The habitat is where it lives; the niche is its full role, including resources used and interactions.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "Conservation of species in their natural habitats, for example by establishing protected areas or nature reserves"?
options: anthropogenic
rewilding
invasive alien species
in situ conservation
items.answer: in situ conservation
items.markingKey: D. This is the definition of in situ conservation.

items.stem: Carp DNA was detected beyond barriers, prompting further monitoring. Which concept is best illustrated by this example (the use of eDNA to track invasive Asian carp in the Great Lakes)?
options: The benefits and limitations of eDNA
The use of whole-genome sequencing
The three-domain system of classification
The difficulty of defining species
items.answer: The benefits and limitations of eDNA
items.markingKey: A. It gives early warning of invasions but positive results may come from boats or birds carrying DNA, not live fish.

items.stem: Why are sequence differences assumed to indicate time since divergence?
options: Mutations occur only during speciation.
Species never change after divergence.
Mutations accumulate at a roughly constant rate over time.
Sequences are identical in all species.
items.answer: Mutations accumulate at a roughly constant rate over time.
items.markingKey: C. This is the basis of the molecular clock.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "analogous structures"?
options: Structures with a similar function and appearance that evolved independently and do not share a common ancestral origin
The rapid divergence of an ancestral species into many species adapted to different niches
A reduced structure that had a function in an ancestor but has little or no function in the present organism
The cumulative change in the heritable characteristics of a population over time
items.answer: Structures with a similar function and appearance that evolved independently and do not share a common ancestral origin
items.markingKey: A. "analogous structures" is structures with a similar function and appearance that evolved independently and do not share a common ancestral origin.

items.stem: Why is the number of possible polypeptides almost unlimited?
options: Each protein contains every amino acid once.
Any of 20 amino acids can occur at each position and chains vary in length.
There are only 20 possible proteins.
Peptide bonds vary in type.
items.answer: Any of 20 amino acids can occur at each position and chains vary in length.
items.markingKey: B. 20ⁿ sequences for a chain of n amino acids.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "realised niche"?
options: The actual range of conditions and resources a species uses when competitors are present
An organism that respires aerobically when oxygen is present but can switch to anaerobic respiration when it is absent
The role of a species in an ecosystem, including its habitat, its use of resources and all its interactions with other species and abiotic factors
The place where a community, species, population or organism lives, described by its geographical and physical location and type of ecosystem
items.answer: The actual range of conditions and resources a species uses when competitors are present
items.markingKey: A. "realised niche" is the actual range of conditions and resources a species uses when competitors are present.

items.stem: A sample of DNA has a higher melting temperature than another of the same length. What is the most likely explanation?
options: It has a higher proportion of A–T base pairs.
It is single-stranded.
It contains uracil instead of thymine.
It has a higher proportion of G–C base pairs.
items.answer: It has a higher proportion of G–C base pairs.
items.markingKey: D. Three hydrogen bonds per G–C pair require more energy to separate.

items.stem: Which statement about muscle contraction: sliding filament model and the skeleton is not correct?
options: The A band contains myosin (with overlapping actin) and stays the same length.
During contraction the actin and myosin filaments get shorter.
Actin is the thin filament protein with binding sites for myosin heads.
Sarcomere is the repeating contractile unit of a myofibril, between two Z lines.
items.answer: During contraction the actin and myosin filaments get shorter.
items.markingKey: B. The incorrect statement is “During contraction the actin and myosin filaments get shorter.” – The filaments stay the same length; they slide past each other so that the sarcomere shortens.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "xylem"?
options: The pacemaker of the heart: a group of specialised cardiac muscle cells in the right atrium that initiates each heartbeat
The volume of blood pumped by one ventricle per minute; stroke volume × heart rate
Pores in the epidermis of leaves, each surrounded by two guard cells, that allow gas exchange and control water loss
Plant tissue of dead, hollow, lignified vessels that transports water and mineral ions from roots to leaves
items.answer: Plant tissue of dead, hollow, lignified vessels that transports water and mineral ions from roots to leaves
items.markingKey: D. "xylem" is plant tissue of dead, hollow, lignified vessels that transports water and mineral ions from roots to leaves.

items.stem: Why is the current biodiversity crisis sometimes called the “sixth mass extinction”?
options: Extinction rates are estimated to be tens to hundreds of times the background rate, comparable with past mass extinctions.
Five mass extinctions were caused by humans.
It was caused by an asteroid.
Exactly five species have become extinct.
items.answer: Extinction rates are estimated to be tens to hundreds of times the background rate, comparable with past mass extinctions.
items.markingKey: A. Rates far exceed background levels.

items.stem: Which evidence supports the endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria?
options: they are made by the Golgi apparatus
they contain cellulose walls
they are found only in plants
they have their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes
items.answer: they have their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes
items.markingKey: D. These are prokaryote-like features.

items.stem: Electric sparks passed through methane, ammonia, hydrogen and water produced several amino acids within a week. Which concept is best illustrated by this example (the Miller–Urey experiment (1953))?
options: The link between ultrastructure and function
Prokaryotic cell structure
The origin of eukaryotic cells by endosymbiosis
How conditions on early Earth may have produced organic molecules
items.answer: How conditions on early Earth may have produced organic molecules
items.markingKey: D. It showed that, with an energy source and a reducing atmosphere, monomers needed for life form spontaneously.

items.stem: Which of these statements about prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell structure; electron micrographs contains a misconception?
options: All plant cells contain chloroplasts.
Prokaryotic cells lack a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, have naked circular DNA, 70S ribosomes and are usually 1–10 µm.
Compartmentalisation is the division of a eukaryotic cell into membrane-bound organelles so that different processes can occur in separate, optimised environments.
70S ribosome is the smaller type of ribosome found in prokaryotes (and mitochondria and chloroplasts).
items.answer: All plant cells contain chloroplasts.
items.markingKey: A. The incorrect statement is “All plant cells contain chloroplasts.” – Only photosynthetic plant cells (e.g. mesophyll) contain chloroplasts; root cells do not.

items.stem: Which channel opens when acetylcholine binds at a neuromuscular junction?
options: the sodium–potassium pump
an aquaporin
a voltage-gated potassium channel
a ligand-gated (nicotinic acetylcholine) channel
items.answer: a ligand-gated (nicotinic acetylcholine) channel
items.markingKey: D. Binding opens a cation channel.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about speciation by reproductive isolation: allopatric and sympatric is false?
options: Any geographical barrier immediately creates new species.
Allopatric speciation occurs when populations are separated by a geographical barrier.
Allopatric speciation is speciation that occurs when populations are separated geographically.
Behavioural isolation is reproductive isolation caused by differences in courtship or mating behaviour.
items.answer: Any geographical barrier immediately creates new species.
items.markingKey: A. The incorrect statement is “Any geographical barrier immediately creates new species.” – The barrier only stops gene flow; speciation follows only after the gene pools diverge enough to cause reproductive isolation.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "Artificial selection in which humans choose individuals with desired traits to breed, changing the characteristics of domesticated species over generations"?
options: sympatric speciation
divergent evolution
hybrid sterility
selective breeding
items.answer: selective breeding
items.markingKey: D. This is the definition of selective breeding.

items.stem: A sample from leaf litter in a Costa Rican forest contained 13 ants, 6 springtails and 13 mites. What is Simpson’s reciprocal index, D = N(N − 1)/Σn(n − 1)?
Why does a potometer only estimate transpiration rate?
options: It measures water uptake, some of which is used in photosynthesis or retained by cells.
It measures oxygen production.
It only works in darkness.
It measures evaporation from the water surface.
items.answer: It measures water uptake, some of which is used in photosynthesis or retained by cells.
items.markingKey: A. Uptake ≈ but not exactly = loss.

items.stem:
In the Hershey–Chase experiment, E. coli infected with radioactively labelled T2 phage were agitated in a blender for different times. The percentage of each isotope released into the supernatant and the percentage of bacteria still infected were measured.

Blending time / min | ³⁵S released / % | ³²P released / %
0 | 0 | 0
1 | 46 | 17
2 | 66 | 23
4 | 78 | 28
6 | 85 | 28
8 | 81 | 28

After 8 minutes 97 % of bacteria were still infected.

(a) State the percentage of ³⁵S released after 4 minutes of blending. [1]
(b) Compare the release of ³⁵S and ³²P during blending. [2]
(c) Explain what the results suggest about the nature of the genetic material. [3]
(d) Suggest why about 20 % of ³⁵S was never released. [1]
(e) Explain why radioactive sulfur and phosphorus were used as labels. [2]
items.answer: (a) 78 % (b) Both rise quickly in the first 2 minutes and then level off; far more ³⁵S (about 81 %) than ³²P (about 28 %) is released. (c) DNA (³²P) mostly remains with/inside the bacteria while protein (³⁵S) is mostly removed; infection continues, so DNA is the material that enters and directs phage production. (d) Some coats remained attached to cells even after blending / some protein entered / incomplete separation in centrifugation. (e) Sulfur is found in proteins (some amino acids) but not DNA; phosphorus is in DNA (phosphate groups) but not in protein, so each label tracks one molecule.
items.markingKey: (a) [1] 78 % (A1). (b) [2] Both increase then plateau (A1); ³⁵S release much greater than ³²P at each time (A1). (c) [3] DNA enters cells (A1); protein stays outside (A1); DNA carries genetic information (R1). (d) [1] Any valid suggestion (A1). (e) [2] S in protein only (A1); P in DNA only (A1).

items.stem:
Samples of a protease from the soil bacterium Bacillus subtilis (enzyme X) and the same enzyme from a hot-spring bacterium (enzyme Y) were held at different temperatures for 10 minutes, cooled to 25 °C and their remaining activity measured as a percentage of the untreated activity.

Temperature / °C | Enzyme X activity remaining / % | Enzyme Y activity remaining / %
30 | 100 | 100
40 | 100 | 100
50 | 94 | 100
60 | 49 | 100
70 | 5 | 97
80 | 0 | 67
90 | 0 | 10

(a) State the activity of enzyme X remaining after treatment at 60 °C. [1]
(b) Estimate the temperature at which each enzyme has lost half of its activity. [2]
(c) Compare the effect of temperature on enzymes X and Y. [2]
(d) Explain why activity was measured at 25 °C after cooling, rather than at the treatment temperature. [1]
(e) Suggest how the structure of enzyme Y differs to make it more heat stable. [1]
(f) Suggest one industrial use of enzyme Y and justify it. [2]
items.answer: (a) 49 % (b) X ≈ 60 °C; Y ≈ 83 °C (c) Both retain full activity at low temperatures and lose activity as temperature rises; Y tolerates much higher temperatures before losing activity. (d) It measures only the permanent (irreversible) loss of activity due to denaturation, not the temporary effect of temperature on reaction rate. (e) More disulfide bonds, ionic bonds (salt bridges) and hydrophobic interactions; more compact core. (f) PCR or biological washing powders/industrial processes at high temperature – remains active and reactions are faster at high temperature.
items.markingKey: (a) [1] 49 % (A1). (b) [2] Interpolation (M1); X 60 °C and Y 83 °C, accept ±2 °C (A1). (c) [2] Similarity (A1); difference with data (A1). (d) [1] Separates denaturation from effect on rate (R1). (e) [1] Any valid structural difference (A1). (f) [2] Use (A1) with justification (R1).

items.stem:
In the late 1940s Erwin Chargaff analysed the base composition of DNA from many organisms. Some of his results (percentage of each base) are shown.

Source of DNA | A | G | C | T
wheat (Triticum aestivum) | 27.3 | 22.7 | 22.8 | 27.1
octopus (Octopus vulgaris) | 33.2 | 17.6 | 17.6 | 31.6
sea urchin (Strongylocentrotus) | 32.8 | 17.7 | 17.3 | 32.1
chicken (Gallus gallus) | 28.0 | 22.0 | 21.6 | 28.4

(a) Calculate the ratio of A to T and of G to C for octopus (Octopus vulgaris). [2]
(b) Identify the organism in the table whose DNA has the highest proportion of G + C. [1]
(c) Explain how these data support the model of DNA proposed by Watson and Crick. [3]
(d) Explain how the data falsify the tetranucleotide hypothesis. [2]
(e) Suggest why the ratios are not exactly 1.00. [1]
items.answer: (a) A/T = 1.05; G/C = 1.00 (b) wheat (Triticum aestivum) (45.5 %) (c) A ≈ T and G ≈ C in each species, consistent with complementary base pairing of A with T and G with C in a double-stranded molecule; purine/pyrimidine ≈ 1 fits one purine pairing with one pyrimidine. (d) The hypothesis predicts 25 % of each base in all DNA; proportions differ markedly between species (e.g. A from about 25 % to over 30 %), so DNA is not a simple repeating unit. (e) Experimental/measurement error in hydrolysis and chromatography; incomplete separation of bases; impurities.
items.markingKey: (a) [2] 33.2/31.6 = 1.05 (A1); 17.6/17.6 = 1.00 (A1). (b) [1] wheat (Triticum aestivum) (A1). (c) [3] A ≈ T and G ≈ C (A1); complementary base pairing (R1); purine with pyrimidine / ratio ≈ 1 (R1). (d) [2] Prediction of 25 % each (A1); observed variation between species (R1). (e) [1] Any valid source of experimental error (A1).

items.stem:
Cubes of agar containing phenolphthalein (pink in alkali) were placed in dilute hydrochloric acid. The time taken for each cube to become completely colourless was recorded.

Side length / cm | SA:V ratio / cm⁻¹ | Time to decolourise / min
0.5 | 12.0 | 0.1
1.0 | 6.0 | 0.2
1.5 | 4.0 | 0.2
2.0 | ? | 0.3
2.5 | 2.4 | 0.4

(a) Calculate the SA:V ratio of the 2.0 cm cube. [2]
(b) Describe the relationship between SA:V ratio and the time taken to decolourise. [1]
(c) Calculate the mean rate of diffusion of acid into the 2.5 cm cube in cm per minute. [2]
(d) Identify two sources of error and suggest improvements. [2]
(e) Suggest why the cubes were fully immersed and not touching the container. [1]
items.answer: (a) 3.0 cm⁻¹ (b) As SA:V ratio decreases (larger cubes), time increases. (c) 3.125 cm min⁻¹ (d) Judging the colour end-point by eye – use a white tile/repeat; inaccurately cut cubes – use a template/measure with calipers; temperature/acid concentration variation – control. (e) So acid can diffuse in through all six faces and SA is as calculated.
items.markingKey: (a) [2] SA = 6 × 2.0² = 24.00; V = 8.000 (M1); ratio 3.0 (A1). (b) [1] Inverse relationship described (A1). (c) [2] Distance to centre = 1.25 cm (M1); 1.25/0.4 = 3.125 cm min⁻¹ (A1). (d) [2] Two errors with improvements (A1 A1). (e) [1] All faces exposed (A1).

items.stem:
A spirometer trace was recorded for Elena, a 17-year-old student, at rest. Values read from the trace are shown.

Lung volume | Value / dm³
tidal volume | 0.52
inspiratory reserve volume | 2.83
expiratory reserve volume | 1.31
residual volume (estimated) | 1.24

During the recording Elena took 12 breaths in one minute.

(a) Calculate the vital capacity. [2]
(b) Calculate the ventilation rate at rest. [1]
(c) Calculate the total lung capacity and the percentage of it that is residual volume. [2]
(d) Explain why residual volume cannot be measured with a simple spirometer. [1]
(e) Predict and explain how tidal volume and breathing rate would change during vigorous exercise. [3]
(f) State two precautions needed when using a spirometer. [2]
(g) Suggest why vital capacity is often lower in smokers. [1]
items.answer: (a) 4.66 dm³ (b) 6.24 dm³ min⁻¹ (c) 5.90 dm³; 21 % (d) It is the air that remains in the lungs after maximum expiration, so it never enters or leaves the spirometer. (e) Both increase; tidal volume uses part of the inspiratory and expiratory reserve volumes; to supply more O₂ and remove more CO₂ produced by respiration. (f) Sterilise the mouthpiece; use a nose clip; ensure soda lime is fresh to absorb CO₂; stop if dizzy; person must be healthy (no asthma). (g) Damage to alveolar walls (emphysema) and narrowing of airways reduces elastic recoil and the volume that can be exhaled.
items.markingKey: (a) [2] VC = TV + IRV + ERV = 0.52 + 2.83 + 1.31 (M1) = 4.66 dm³ (A1). (b) [1] 0.52 × 12 = 6.24 dm³ min⁻¹ (A1). (c) [2] 4.66 + 1.24 = 5.90 (A1); 1.24/5.90 × 100 = 21 % (A1). (d) [1] Air never exhaled (A1). (e) [3] Both increase (A1); reserve volumes used (A1); link to respiration/CO₂ (R1). (f) [2] Two valid precautions (A1 A1). (g) [1] Valid reason (A1).

items.stem:
This question is about water as the medium for life: hydrogen bonding and polarity.

(a) Which atom in a water molecule carries a partial negative charge? [1]

(b) Explain why a water molecule is polar. [2]

(c) "Water is polar because the molecule carries an overall negative charge." Explain the flaw in this statement. [3]
items.answer: (a) oxygen (b) Oxygen is more electronegative than hydrogen, so the shared electrons in each O–H bond are pulled towards oxygen; oxygen becomes δ− and the hydrogens δ+; because the molecule is bent, the charges do not cancel, giving a dipole. (c) Water is electrically neutral overall; it is polar because charge is unevenly distributed (δ− oxygen, δ+ hydrogens) owing to oxygen’s electronegativity and the bent shape.
items.markingKey: (a) [1] oxygen. Oxygen is more electronegative than hydrogen, so it pulls the shared electrons towards itself and becomes δ−. Award up to 1 mark for valid, linked points. (b) [2] Award marks for: Oxygen is more electronegative than hydrogen, so the shared electrons in each O–H bond are pulled towards oxygen; oxygen becomes δ− and the hydrogens δ+; because the molecule is bent, the charges do not cancel, giving a dipole. Award up to 2 marks for valid, linked points. (c) [3] Water is electrically neutral overall; it is polar because charge is unevenly distributed (δ− oxygen, δ+ hydrogens) owing to oxygen’s electronegativity and the bent shape. Award up to 3 marks for valid, linked points.

items.stem:
This question is about origin of water on Earth and the search for extraterrestrial life.

(a) A student claims: "Water has always been on Earth because it formed from the same material as the planet in a hot state." Identify the error in this claim and correct it. [2]

(b) The habitable (Goldilocks) zone of the Sun lies between about 0.95 AU and 1.37 AU. The distance of the zone scales with the square root of a star’s luminosity. a K-type star has a luminosity 0.25 times that of the Sun. Calculate the inner and outer limits of its habitable zone. [4]
items.answer: (a) The early Earth was very hot and much water would have been lost; much of the present water is thought to have been delivered later by water-rich asteroids. (b) 0.47 AU to 0.69 AU
items.markingKey: (a) [2] The early Earth was very hot and much water would have been lost; much of the present water is thought to have been delivered later by water-rich asteroids. Award up to 2 marks for valid, linked points. (b) [4] √0.25 = 0.50 (M1); inner = 0.95 × 0.50 = 0.47 AU, outer = 1.37 × 0.50 = 0.69 AU (A1). Award up to 4 marks for valid, linked points.

items.stem:
This question is about carbon compounds and condensation and hydrolysis reactions.

(a) State what is meant by the term "macromolecule". [1]

(b) Hana writes: "Hydrolysis releases water as large molecules are broken down." Explain why this is inaccurate. [2]

(c) Briefly describe the digestion of starch in bread and explain what it reveals about hydrolysis reactions. [3]
items.answer: (a) A very large molecule such as a polysaccharide, polypeptide or nucleic acid (b) Hydrolysis uses (consumes) water to break bonds; it is condensation that releases water. (c) Salivary and pancreatic amylase hydrolyse starch into maltose, which maltase then hydrolyses to glucose. Water is added to break each glycosidic bond, converting the polymer into absorbable monomers.
items.markingKey: (a) [1] a very large molecule such as a polysaccharide, polypeptide or nucleic acid. Award up to 1 mark for valid, linked points. (b) [2] Hydrolysis uses (consumes) water to break bonds; it is condensation that releases water. Award up to 2 marks for valid, linked points. (c) [3] Context (Salivary and pancreatic amylase hydrolyse starch into maltose, which maltase then hydrolyses to glucose.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Water is added to break each glycosidic bond, converting the polymer into absorbable monomers. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to hydrolysis reactions. Award up to 3 marks for valid, linked points.

items.stem:
This question is about fibrous and globular proteins and form-function relationships.

(a) Outline the meaning of the term "insulin". [1]

(b) A student claims: "All proteins are enzymes." Identify the error in this claim and correct it. [2]

(c) Briefly describe scurvy in sailors on long voyages in the 18th century and explain what it reveals about the structure and function of collagen. [3]
items.answer: (a) A small globular hormone of two polypeptide chains linked by disulfide bonds, which binds to receptors to lower blood glucose (b) Proteins have many roles: structural (collagen), hormones (insulin), transport (haemoglobin), defence (antibodies), movement (actin/myosin) as well as enzymes. (c) Lack of vitamin C caused bleeding gums, reopening of old wounds and weakened tissues. Vitamin C is needed to stabilise collagen; without it, collagen fibres are weak, showing the importance of structure for function.
items.markingKey: (a) [1] a small globular hormone of two polypeptide chains linked by disulfide bonds, which binds to receptors to lower blood glucose. Award up to 1 mark for valid, linked points. (b) [2] Proteins have many roles: structural (collagen), hormones (insulin), transport (haemoglobin), defence (antibodies), movement (actin/myosin) as well as enzymes. Award up to 2 marks for valid, linked points. (c) [3] Context (Lack of vitamin C caused bleeding gums, reopening of old wounds and weakened tissues.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. (c) With reference to mRNA vaccines against COVID-19, explain how it illustrates the structural differences between RNA and DNA. [3]
items.answer: (a) DNA is double-stranded and RNA is single-stranded. (b) RNA is single-stranded but can fold and base-pair with itself, e.g. tRNA forms a clover-leaf shape and rRNA forms part of ribosome structure. (c) Lipid nanoparticles deliver mRNA coding for the spike protein; cells translate it and the mRNA is soon degraded. The instability of single-stranded RNA means it does not persist or enter the nucleus, so it is translated briefly then broken down.

This question is about habitats, adaptations and abiotic variables.

(a) Explain how marram grass is adapted to sand dunes. [4]

(b) "Animals develop adaptations during their lifetime because they need them." Explain the flaw in this statement. [5]

(c) "Abiotic factors are more important than biotic factors in determining the distribution of species." Discuss. [7]
items.answer: (a) Leaves roll up with stomata on the inner surface in pits with hairs, trapping humid air and reducing transpiration; thick cuticle on the outer surface; long roots reach deep water; rhizomes grow upward when buried by sand. (b) Adaptations arise by natural selection on heritable variation over generations; individuals do not develop them in response to need. (c) Abiotic factors determine where species could live (fundamental range), but biotic interactions often determine where they actually live.
